title: Plate configuration
description: A floor plate: the file the drawing is made from. A file with a `start` is a plate; one without is a plan to import, shown on its own in a preview slot.
$comment: This file is the single definition of the configuration format: the engine compiles it to Nickel contracts, and the editor reads it for hover docs, completions and the reference panel.

name.description: Name of the floor plate. Shown in the drawing's title block and written into exports.

system.description: How lengths are shown: metres, or feet and inches. Also sets the default `units` and the export paper scale (1:100, or 1/8" = 1'-0").

x-enumDescriptions.metric: Lengths in metres, areas in m², printed at 1:100.
x-enumDescriptions.imperial: Lengths in feet and inches, areas in ft², printed at 1/8" = 1'-0".

units.description: Unit of plain numbers such as the 30 in `[30, 0]`. Defaults to `'m` for metric and `'ft` for imperial. Lengths written as strings carry their own unit.

start.description: The geometry the solver starts from, chosen by `mode`: a closed `'boundary` that everything stays inside, or a `'spine` the solver works around. A spine with a single point is a free origin.

seed.description: Seed for the solver. The same file and seed always give the same layout; change it to see another solution.

grid.description: Grid the solver snaps spaces to. Defaults to 0.25 m (metric) or 9" (imperial), and finer in a plan with small fixtures (down to 100 mm or 4"). Smaller is finer but slower.

height.description: Floor to ceiling. Services use it for the cable that runs up a wall to the ceiling and down again. Defaults to 2.4 m (metric) or 8 ft (imperial).

Start.description: The geometry the solver starts from, chosen by `mode`.
x-examples:
# Free: a spine with a single point, the origin.
start = { mode = 'spine, points = [[0, 0]] },

BoundaryStart.description: A closed boundary. Everything the solver places stays inside it.

mode.description: How the solver uses the starting geometry.

points.description: Corners of the boundary, in order, as [x, y]. The last connects back to the first.
points.errorMessage: a boundary needs at least 3 points, each written [x, y]

ports.description: Port roles of the boundary's edges, in order: the first is the edge from point 1 to point 2. Edges not listed are `'facade`.
x-examples:
# One role per edge: point 1 to 2, 2 to 3, …
ports = ['facade, 'blank, 'facade, ['party, 'wet]],

SpineStart.description: A spine: a line the solver works around. With a single point it is a free origin.

mode.description: How the solver uses the starting geometry.

points.description: Points along the spine, in order, as [x, y]. A single point is a free origin.
points.errorMessage: a spine needs at least 1 point, each written [x, y]

Point.description: A point, written [x, y]. Each coordinate is a length: a number in `units`, or a string such as "98'-6" or "9.5 m".

Length.description: A length: a number in `units`, or a string with its own unit, such as "98'-6", "12 ft 6 in", "9.5 m" or "950 mm".
Length.errorMessage: expected a length: a number, or a string such as "98'-6", "12 ft 6 in", "9.5 m" or "950 mm"
x-examples:
["98'-6", 0],         # feet and inches
["98 ft 6 1/2 in", 0],
["9.5 m", "950 mm"],  # units can be mixed

EdgeRoles.description: The role of one edge: a port role such as `'facade` or `'blank`, or several, such as `['party, 'wet]`.
EdgeRoles.errorMessage: expected a port role such as 'facade, or a list of them

Port.description: A port role: what an edge of a space's boundary is for. Dotted roles refine a core one: `'facade.storefront` is a kind of `'facade`.
Port.errorMessage: expected a port role such as 'entrance, 'facade or 'wet

x-enumDescriptions.entrance: Primary way in, from the parent's circulation. A door goes here.
x-enumDescriptions.link: Optional connection to a sibling, like connecting hotel rooms.
x-enumDescriptions.blank: Exterior wall that can't have openings (lot line, fire wall).
x-enumDescriptions.outdoor: Opens onto a balcony, terrace or courtyard.
x-enumDescriptions.party: Wall shared with a sibling unit. No openings.
x-enumDescriptions.partition: Ordinary interior wall to another space.
x-enumDescriptions.wet: Plumbing wall: put bathrooms and kitchens against it.
x-enumDescriptions.core: Wall against the building core (lifts, stairs).
x-enumDescriptions.up: Where a stair or lift arrives from below.
x-enumDescriptions.down: Where a stair or lift goes down.
x-enumDescriptions.door: Where a door opens into the space, given by the parent: just the door, not the whole wall. Fixtures keep its swing clear.
x-enumDescriptions.window: Where a window is, given by the parent: just the window, not the whole wall. Keep things off it with `plate.apart "bed" 'window`.

Engine.description: How this plan's spaces are placed. `'grid` packs them inside the boundary; `'spine_stack` lines them up along a corridor. Defaults to `'grid`, or `'spine_stack` when the plate starts from a spine.

x-enumDescriptions.grid: Pack rectangles on a grid inside the slot, maximising the goals.
x-enumDescriptions.spine_stack: A corridor along the spine (or the slot's long axis) with spaces stacked on both sides, like a hotel floor.

Plan.description: A plan: spaces, the rules between them and the goals to maximise. Put a plan in a space (`plan = …`) and it is solved inside that space, as many levels deep as you like. A file that is a plan is shown on its own, in its `preview` slot.

grid.description: Grid the solver snaps spaces to. Defaults to the parent's.

Spaces.description: The spaces to place, by name. The name is how rules refer to a space; repeated spaces are numbered `room_1`, `room_2`, … by position.

Space.description: A space: a room, a corridor, a void, a stair, or a fixture (a bed, a counter, a pool…). Sizes are ranges; the solver picks the rest.

kind.description: What sort of space this is.

x-enumDescriptions.zone: An area with no walls of its own: the desks of an open-plan office, the dining end of an open living room. It's placed like a room and can have a plan, but its edges that face open floor (a fill space or another zone) are 'open, not walls: fixtures don't back onto them.
x-enumDescriptions.circulation: A corridor or hall people move through.
x-enumDescriptions.void: A hole, courtyard or light well.
x-enumDescriptions.fixture: Something that takes up floor and holds nothing else: a bed, a counter, an island, a pool, a parking stall. It has a front, can keep clear floor around it (`clearance`), and can't have a plan.

label.description: Display name, e.g. "Master bedroom". Defaults to the space's name.

count.description: How many: a whole number, or `{ min, max }` to let the solver decide.

fill.description: Takes the floor the other spaces leave, whatever its shape: a hall that reaches every room, an open-plan floor around meeting rooms, a garden around a house. Its sizes still count (`area`, and `side.min` as its narrowest width), and rules can name it (`plate.door "bedroom" "hall"`). At most one per plan, and it can't be pinned with `at`. It can have a `plan`, solved in its real shape.
x-examples: hall = { kind = 'circulation, fill = true, area = { min = 8, max = 16 }, side.min = 1.2 },

at.description: Fixes the space in place: the corner nearest the origin (its lower left), or one corner per instance. In a plate, in the plate's coordinates; in a plan, from the lower-left corner of its slot with the entrance along the bottom (as its preview shows it). Needs an exact `width` (along x) and `depth` (along y). For what's already there: a core, a stair, columns.
at.errorMessage: expected a corner [x, y], or a list of them

walls.description: Port roles this space's walls give the spaces next to it. A bathroom with `walls = 'wet` makes a 'wet edge in the kitchen beside it, so a plan there can put the sink against it (`against = 'wet`).

area.description: Floor area, in square `units`: a number (exact) or `{ min, max }`.

side.description: Length of every side: `{ min, max }`.

width.description: Width: along the corridor or entrance; for a fixture, along its front. A length (exact) or `{ min, max }`.

depth.description: Depth: away from the corridor or entrance; for a fixture, from its front to its back. A length (exact) or `{ min, max }`.

aspect.description: Longest side divided by the shortest, at most.

plan.description: A plan solved inside this space once it is placed. Not for fixtures: a fixture is the last level.

clearance.description: Fixtures only: clear floor kept on its sides, where nothing else may stand. One length all round, or `{ front, back, left, right }` (left and right as seen standing at the front, facing it). Clearances of different fixtures may overlap: they share the walkway.

against.description: Fixtures only: its back goes against an edge of the space it's in. `'wall` for any edge, or a port role such as `'wet` or `'facade` for that kind of edge.
x-examples: against = 'wet,  # a vanity on the plumbing wall

row.description: Fixtures only: place the instances side by side in one straight run, fronts in line, like a bench of desks, a row of seats or a run of parking bays. Needs an exact `count`.
x-examples: desk = { kind = 'fixture, count = 3, row = true, width = 1.6, depth = 0.8, clearance.front = 1, symbol = 'desk },

symbol.description: A drawing to show it with, from the symbol catalog: a bed, a car, a pool… It's drawn from the front (a fixture's front, or the side a room is entered from) and fitted to the space. It only changes the drawing, never the solution.

typical.description: Repeated spaces with the same shape and ports share one solution of their plan (a typical). Set false to solve each one separately.

mirror.description: Typical copies may be mirrored to fit. Set false to only rotate them.

tags.description: Labels that rules and services pick it by, whatever it's called: `tags = ['sleep]` and `"#sleep"` selects it. Dotted like port roles: `'wet.shower` is a kind of `'wet`. Its `kind` counts as a tag too (`"#room"`, `"#circulation"`, `"#fixture"`).
x-examples: tags = ['water, 'drain],  # a toilet, for the plumbing

load.description: Fixtures: what it asks of each service, by service name: `load.power = { current = "40 A", voltage = 240, conductors = 3 }`. A part placed on it (`plate.on`) carries it. Only how it's served: never changes the layout.

x-examples: bedroom = { count = 2, area = { min = 11, max = 16 }, side.min = 2.8 },
bed = { kind = 'fixture, width = 1.6, depth = 2.1, against = 'wall, clearance = { front = 0.9, left = 0.6, right = 0.6 }, symbol = 'bed_queen },

Clearance.description: Clear floor around a fixture: a length on every side, or `{ front, back, left, right }` with a length for each side that needs one (the others get none).

front.description: In front of it: where you stand to use it.

left.description: On its left, seen from the front.

right.description: On its right, seen from the front.

Clearance.errorMessage: expected a length, or { front, back, left, right } with lengths

Symbol.description: A drawing from the symbol catalog (`schema/symbols.json`). Indoors and out: furniture, kitchens and bathrooms, vehicles, gardens, pools and courts.

x-enumDescriptions.receptacle_240: 240 V receptacle (services), 150 × 100 mm: a range, a dryer

Symbol.errorMessage: expected a symbol from the catalog, such as 'bed_queen, 'sofa or 'car

Count.description: How many: a whole number, or `{ min, max }` to let the solver decide.
Count.errorMessage: expected a count: a whole number, or { min, max }

LengthRange.description: A length (exact) or a range `{ min, max }`.
LengthRange.errorMessage: expected a length, or { min, max } with lengths

AreaRange.description: An area (exact) or a range `{ min, max }`, in square `units`.
AreaRange.errorMessage: expected an area, or { min, max }

Needs.description: What this plan needs from the space it is placed in. The parent sizes the space to fit, and the plan rejects a space that doesn't.

width.description: Width of the space, along its entrance.

depth.description: Depth of the space, away from its entrance.

ports.description: Port roles the space must have, may have, or must not have, e.g. `{ entrance = 'required, blank = 'forbidden }`.

PortNeed.description: Whether a port role must be present.

x-enumDescriptions.required: The space must have this port.
x-enumDescriptions.forbidden: The space must not have this port.

Preview.description: How the plan is shown when its file is opened on its own: the slot it is solved in, as a plate would solve it in a space of that size with those ports. One slot, or a list of named ones to switch between. Ignored when the plan is used in a space.
Preview.errorMessage: expected a preview slot { width, depth, ports }, or a list of them
x-examples:
preview = [
  { name = "standard", width = 3.8, depth = 8.2 },
  { name = "corner", width = 4.2, depth = 8.2, ports.left = 'facade },
],

PreviewCase.description: A rectangular slot to preview the plan in, entrance along the bottom by default. Sizes left out are picked from `needs`.

name.description: What this slot is, shown in the preview's menu, e.g. "corner".

width.description: Width of the slot, along its bottom edge. Picked from `needs.width` when left out.

depth.description: Depth of the slot, away from its bottom edge. Picked from `needs.depth` when left out.

system.description: How lengths are shown, and the default `units`, while previewing. A plate using the plan decides this for itself.

units.description: Unit of plain numbers while previewing. Defaults from `system`. A plate using the plan decides this for itself.

seed.description: Seed for the preview's solution. A plate using the plan solves it with its own seed.

SidePorts.description: Port roles of the slot's four sides. Sides left out are those of a typical room on a corridor: `'entrance` at the bottom, `'facade` at the top, `'party` on the right and `['party, 'wet]` on the left.

Goals.description: What makes one solution better than another once every required rule holds. Each goal has a weight; 0 turns it off.

utilization.description: Cover as much of the available floor as possible.

compactness.description: Prefer square-ish spaces over long thin ones.

Rules.description: Rules between spaces. Write them with the `plate` helpers, e.g. `plate.door "bedroom" "hall"`. A rule is required unless it has a `weight` (see `plate.prefer`).

RuleItem.description: A rule, or a list of rules (helpers such as `plate.between` return several).

Selector.description: Which spaces: a name (`"kitchen"`), a space type (`"bedroom"` matches every bedroom), a pattern (`"bed*"`), a tag (`"#sleep"`), or a list of these.
Selector.errorMessage: expected a space name such as "kitchen", or a list of names
x-examples:
plate.door "bedroom" "hall"        # every bedroom
plate.window "bed*"                # a pattern
plate.apart ["bath", "wc"] "kitchen" # a list

RuleTouch.description: Each `a` shares a wall with a `b` (or with a port of the parent space).

a.description: The spaces the rule applies to; each of them must satisfy it.

b.description: The other side; any one of them will do.

port.description: A port of the space this plan is placed in, instead of a space.

each.description: With `port`: meet every separate stretch of that port, not just one. A plan between two wings, say, reaches the 'link on both sides: `plate.touches "gallery" 'link & { each = true }`.

length.description: Shortest shared wall. Defaults to 1 m (3 ft), or 0.3 m (1 ft) when `a` is a fixture.

weight.description: Makes the rule a preference: how much it matters compared with the goals. Leave out for a required rule.

RuleApart.description: No `a` touches a `b` (or a port of the parent space, such as `'window`): no shared wall, and at least `distance` between them when given.

a.description: The spaces the rule applies to; each of them must satisfy it.

b.description: The spaces to keep away from; every one of them.

port.description: A port of the space this plan is placed in, instead of a space: `'window` keeps clear of its windows, `'door` of its doors, `'facade` of its outside walls.

distance.description: Smallest gap to keep, between the closest points. Leave out to only forbid touching.

wall.description: With a port: keep off the whole wall the port is on, not just the port itself. `plate.apart "bed" 'window & { wall = true }` keeps the bed off any wall with a window.

weight.description: Makes the rule a preference: how much it matters compared with the goals. Leave out for a required rule.

RuleDoor.description: Each `a` has a door to a `b` (or to a port of the parent space, such as `'entrance`).

a.description: The spaces the rule applies to; each of them must satisfy it.

b.description: The other side; any one of them will do.

port.description: A port of the space this plan is placed in, instead of a space.

each.description: With `port`: meet every separate stretch of that port, not just one. A plan between two wings, say, reaches the 'link on both sides: `plate.touches "gallery" 'link & { each = true }`.

width.description: Door width. Defaults to 0.9 m (3 ft).

weight.description: Makes the rule a preference: how much it matters compared with the goals. Leave out for a required rule.

RuleWindow.description: Each `a` has a window on a port of the parent space, `'facade` unless given.

a.description: The spaces the rule applies to; each of them must satisfy it.

port.description: A port of the space this plan is placed in, instead of a space.

width.description: Window width. Defaults to 1.2 m (4 ft).

weight.description: Makes the rule a preference: how much it matters compared with the goals. Leave out for a required rule.

RuleNear.description: Each `a` is within `distance` of a `b` (between their closest walls).

a.description: The spaces the rule applies to; each of them must satisfy it.

b.description: The other side; any one of them will do.

weight.description: Makes the rule a preference: how much it matters compared with the goals. Leave out for a required rule.

RuleFaces.description: Each `a` (a fixture) faces a `b`: the `b` is in front of it and across from its front. A sofa facing the TV, a desk facing the window side, chairs facing a table.

a.description: The fixtures the rule applies to; each of them must satisfy it.

b.description: What they face; any one of them will do.

weight.description: Makes the rule a preference: how much it matters compared with the goals. Leave out for a required rule.

RuleReach.description: Going through doors from `a` to `b` always passes through `via`.

a.description: The spaces the rule applies to; each of them must satisfy it.

b.description: The other side; any one of them will do.

via.description: The space in between, such as a hall.

weight.description: Makes the rule a preference: how much it matters compared with the goals. Leave out for a required rule.

RuleAlong.description: `a` spaces line up along the corridor `b` (spine_stack engine).

a.description: The spaces the rule applies to; each of them must satisfy it.

sides.description: Which sides of the corridor to use.

RuleUnique.description: These instances are solved on their own instead of sharing their typical.

a.description: The spaces the rule applies to; each of them must satisfy it.

RuleInstance.description: Give particular instances a different plan.

a.description: The spaces the rule applies to; each of them must satisfy it.

Tag.description: A tag: a label rules and services select spaces by, as `"#tag"`.
Tag.errorMessage: expected a tag such as 'sleep or 'wet.shower

Assemblies.description: What the edges between spaces are built as, by name. Each wall gets the thinnest assembly that meets every requirement on it: those of the assemblies its port roles call for (`on`), and those of `wall` rules. An assembly takes floor: the spaces either side are what its thickness leaves them, and the plans inside them are solved in that. Plans inside inherit these; a plan that names one the same replaces it for itself.

Assembly.description: A wall type: how thick it is, what it holds, how it's rated.

label.description: Display name, e.g. "Exterior wall". Defaults to its name.

on.description: The port roles it's for: walls with any of them call for it. Leave out for one that's only used when a `wall` rule asks for it (by name, or because it's the thinnest that meets what the rule asks).

thickness.description: Overall thickness. Leave out to add up `layers`.

cavity.description: Depth inside it that services can run in (a stud bay). Defaults to the `layers` marked `cavity`, else none.

layers.description: Its build-up, from one face to the other. Thickness and cavity add up from it.

line.description: Where the edge runs through it, on the plate's boundary: `'inside` (the default) puts the boundary on its outside face, so it grows inward; `'centre` straddles it (a party wall on a lot line). Between spaces a wall is always centred.

x-enumDescriptions.inside: The boundary is its outside face.
x-enumDescriptions.centre: The boundary runs down its middle.

pattern.description: How it's hatched in the drawing. Only how it's drawn.

x-enumDescriptions.hatch: Diagonal lines: a stud wall, insulation.
x-enumDescriptions.light: Filled light: a thin or glazed partition.

layer.description: CAD layer it's exported on. Defaults to `A-WALL-` and its name.

cross.description: Whether services' runs may pass through or run in it. Defaults to `'firestop` for a wall with a `fire` rating, else `'yes`.

x-enumDescriptions.firestop: Through a sealed penetration, marked on the drawing: a fire separation.
x-enumDescriptions.no: Never: nothing runs in it or through it.

x-examples: partition = { on = 'partition, thickness = "115 mm", cavity = "89 mm" },

party = {
  on = ['party, 'blank],
  line = 'centre,
  fire = 1,
  acoustic = 55,
  layers = [
    { material = "gypsum", thickness = "16 mm" },
    { material = "stud", thickness = "89 mm", cavity = true },
    { material = "air", thickness = "25 mm" },
    { material = "stud", thickness = "89 mm", cavity = true },
    { material = "gypsum", thickness = "16 mm" },
  ],
  pattern = 'hatch,
},

Layer.description: One layer of an assembly's build-up.

cavity.description: Open space services can run in.

Services.description: Services that run through the spaces and their walls (power, lighting, heat, plumbing, air), by name. A service never builds anything: it claims what it needs (rules and spaces the solver makes room for), places its parts on the solved walls, floors and ceilings, and connects them. Plans inside inherit these; a plan that names one the same replaces it for itself.

Service.description: A service: its parts, what it claims, where its parts go and how they connect.

label.description: Display name, e.g. "Power". Defaults to its name.

scope.description: The spaces it lives in, one network each (`"#dwelling"`: a panel per flat). Its claims apply inside them. Leave out for the whole plan it's declared in.

params.description: Values the service is written in terms of, such as a code's numbers. Refer to them in the service (`params.wall_spacing`) and override them by merging: `(import "build/services/power.ncl") & (import "build/codes/nec.ncl")`. Give them `| default` so a merge can replace them. The solver doesn't read them.

parts.description: What it places, by name: outlets, lights, registers…

place.description: Where its parts go. Write them with the `plate` helpers: `plate.every`, `plate.beside`, `plate.over`, `plate.on`, `plate.one`. Only how parts are drawn: never changes the layout.

connect.description: Networks joining its parts back to a source: circuits, ducts, drains.

feeds.description: Requirements on how some terminals are served: `plate.feed "#cooking" & { medium = "6/3" }`. Only how they're connected: never changes the layout.

Part.description: Something a service places: on a wall, a ceiling or a floor. It takes no floor (a furnace that does is a fixture: claim it).

label.description: Display name. Defaults to its name.

x-enumDescriptions.wall: On the face of a wall, `above` the floor.
x-enumDescriptions.ceiling: On the ceiling: a light, a diffuser.
x-enumDescriptions.floor: On the floor: a register. Kept off fixtures.
x-enumDescriptions.cavity: Inside a wall: a stack, a riser. Fixtures can stand in front of it; the wall's cavity must be as deep as it.

width.description: Along the wall (or across). Defaults to its symbol's size.

depth.description: Out from the wall. Defaults to its symbol's size.

above.description: Height of its middle above the floor, for wall parts. Defaults to 300 mm. Parts at heights at least 300 mm apart can share a stretch of wall.

symbol.description: How it's drawn, from the symbol catalog (its Services drawings).

load.description: What it draws from the network it's on: `{ watts = 1000, voltage = 240 }`. A part placed `on` a fixture without one takes the fixture's `load`.

Claims.description: What the service needs the layout to make room for. Claims are solved: the solver treats them like rules written in each plan.

rules.description: Rules added to every plan in the service's scope. Name spaces by tag (`"#wet"`): a tag no space has is simply not there.

inside.description: Plan pieces merged into the plan of each space a key selects: spaces (a furnace), rules, needs. A space without a plan gets one.

PlaceEvery.description: Along each wall run of the spaces (their perimeter, cut at doorways): at most `spacing` apart, and half that from each end. When it names fixtures, along their backs.

part.description: The part to place, by name.

spaces.description: The spaces (or fixtures) whose walls it lines.

min_run.description: Runs shorter than this get none.

PlaceBeside.description: Beside each door of the spaces (by its latch, or its hinges), or under each window.

part.description: The part to place, by name.

spaces.description: The spaces whose openings it's by. Leave out for every space.

side.description: Which side. Defaults to `'latch` for a door and `'under` for a window.

x-enumDescriptions.latch: Beside a door, on the side it opens from.
x-enumDescriptions.hinge: Beside a door, on its hinge side.
x-enumDescriptions.under: Under it, centred, as wide as it unless the part has a width.

offset.description: Gap from the opening's edge. Defaults to 150 mm.

PlaceOver.description: In the spaces, on the ceiling or floor: one in the middle of the biggest part of each, or spread over all of it. A space that isn't a rectangle (an L, a U) is cut into rectangles and each gets its share: a grid, or a line where it's narrow. A selector that names fixtures puts them over the fixtures instead (pendants over an island).

part.description: The part to place, by name.

spaces.description: The spaces, or fixtures to put them over.

count.description: How many in each space: exactly, or `{ min, max }` to bound what `spacing` or `per` gives. Without `spacing` or `per`, one.

per.description: Floor area each covers (m²): as many as that takes, spread over the space.

spacing.description: At most this far apart, and about half that from the walls: a grid in each part of the space, a line where a part is narrower than this.

layout.description: How they're arranged in each part of the space. Defaults to `'grid`.

x-enumDescriptions.grid: A grid as close to square as fits; a part too narrow for two rows gets a line.
x-enumDescriptions.centre: One in the middle of each part (an L gets two).

margin.description: Never closer than this to a wall, where the share of each leaves room for it. Defaults to 300 mm.

x-examples: plate.over "downlight" "#kitchen" & { spacing = "1.5 m", count = { min = 2, max = 8 } },

PlaceOn.description: One at the back of each fixture: a dedicated outlet, a supply.

part.description: The part to place, by name.

PlaceOne.description: The best single place in each space, on its walls: as near as can be to `near`, away from `apart`.

part.description: The part to place, by name.

near.description: As close as can be to these: a port role (`'entrance`), `'door`, `'window`, or a tag of a fixture (`"#drain"`).

apart.description: Away from these (600 mm or more), and never on a wall with one of these port roles (`'facade`).

wall.description: What the wall it goes on must be.

Requirement.description: What a wall must at least be.

cavity.description: A cavity at least this deep.

fire.description: At least this many hours' fire resistance.

Network.description: A network: parts joined back to a source in groups (circuits), or switches joined to what they control. Drawn along the walls and ceilings it runs in, or as the schematic.

from.description: The source: a part of this service (`"panel"`), or a tagged fixture (`"#air"`). One per scope.

to.description: What it joins: parts of this service (`"outlet"`), of another (`"heat.baseboard"`), or tagged fixtures (`"#drain"`).

max.description: Most in one group (a circuit). Leave out for one group.

limit.description: Longest run from the source (a drain to its stack, a duct).

draw.description: Which drawing exports keep. Both are made: press A in a service view to switch.

x-enumDescriptions.arcs: The electrical convention: an arc from part to part, a numbered home run toward the source.
x-enumDescriptions.routed: Where it runs: in the walls (low, and up over doors), across ceilings, through walls.

x-enumDescriptions.feed: Groups of terminals, each joined back to the source: circuits.
x-enumDescriptions.control: In each room, the sources (switches) joined to the terminals (lights) they control: switch legs. The lights' load goes on the first switch's circuit.

rating.description: Each group's breaker. With loads, a group is also cut so it carries at most 80 % of it.

dedicated.description: One terminal per group: dedicated circuits.

medium.description: The medium every group is made of, by name. Leave out to pick the thinnest that meets each group's breaker and conductors.

x-examples: { from = "stack", to = "#drain", via.cavity = "140 mm", limit = "3 m", draw = 'routed },
{ label = "Counter", from = "panel", to = "counter", rating = "20 A", max = 2 },
{ label = "Switch legs", role = 'control, from = "switch", to = "light", via.ceilings = "#room" },

cavity.description: In walls with a cavity at least this deep. Leave out for any wall.

ceilings.description: Across the ceilings of these spaces. With it a network also runs high in the walls, over doors, and reaches ceiling parts from above; low in the walls it stops at doors. Without it, it runs in the walls only.

RuleWall.description: The walls between `a` and `b` (or `a`'s walls with a port role: `'wall` is all of them) are built as `assembly`, or at least to what the rule asks. With `length`, one stretch that long and clear of doors is enough.

a.description: The spaces the rule applies to; each of them must satisfy it.

b.description: The spaces on the other side.

port.description: Instead of `b`: the walls of `a` with this port role, `'wall` for all of them.

cavity.description: With a cavity at least this deep.

fire.description: At least this many hours' fire resistance.

length.description: One stretch this long, clear of doors, is enough (a duct's stud bay).

weight.description: Makes the rule a preference: how much it matters compared with the goals. Leave out for a required rule.

Current.description: A current in amps: a number, or a string with its unit, such as "30 A".
Current.errorMessage: expected a current: a number of amps, or a string such as "30 A"

Load.description: What a terminal asks of a service: for power, the circuit it needs (from its spec sheet), or its watts, at a voltage. Its circuit's breaker and cable are sized from it.

current.description: The circuit it needs, as its spec sheet says: `"30 A"` for a dryer. A part with one on a dedicated circuit gets that breaker.

watts.description: Or its power, in watts: it draws `watts / voltage`.

conductors.description: Conductors its cable needs, not counting the ground: 3 for a range or a dryer (two hots and a neutral), 2 for a heater on 240 V.

x-examples: load.power = { current = "30 A", voltage = 240, conductors = 3 },  # a dryer
load = { watts = 1000, voltage = 240 },  # a baseboard heater

Medium.description: One kind of thing a service's networks are made of: a cable (`"14/2"`), later a pipe or a duct. Each group of a network gets the thinnest one that meets its breaker and the conductors it needs.

label.description: Display name, e.g. "NM-B 14/2". Defaults to its name.

rating.description: The most it carries: for a cable, the largest breaker it may be on. Check the ampacity table of the code you build to.

conductors.description: Conductors, not counting the ground: the `2` of `14/2`.

colour.description: Its jacket's colour, as runs of it are drawn.

x-enumDescriptions.white: NM-B and NMD90 14 AWG; NMD90 8 AWG and larger.

layer.description: CAD layer its runs are exported on. Defaults to the service's run layer.

Media.description: Media by name: `"14/2"`, `"10/3"`. Keep them in a library file (`build/media/nm-b.ncl`) and merge it in.

Feed.description: A requirement on how some terminals are served: their own circuit, a breaker, a cable. Write it with `plate.feed`. Only how they're connected: never changes the layout.

feed.description: The terminals: parts (`"dedicated"`, `"heat.baseboard"`) or the fixtures they're on (`"fridge"`, `"#cooking"`).

network.description: Only on the network with this label.

rating.description: The breaker their circuit is on.

medium.description: The medium their circuit is made of, by name: `"8/3"`. Leave out to pick the thinnest that does.
